subject: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
description: This course introduces fundamental techniques for designing and analyzing algorithms. It focuses on problem-solving strategies, algorithm efficiency, and complexity analysis for various computational problems.
objectives: Understand the principles and strategies for algorithm design.
Analyze algorithm efficiency using time and space complexity.
Apply various algorithmic paradigms such as divide and conquer, greedy, dynamic programming, and backtracking.
Develop efficient algorithms for real-world problems.
course_outcomes: Define and analyze the asymptotic performance of algorithms.
Apply fundamental algorithmic techniques to solve computational problems.
Design algorithms using divide and conquer, greedy, and dynamic programming approaches.
Understand graph algorithms and their applications.
Classify computational problems into P, NP, and NP-complete categories.

modules.title: Introduction and Asymptotic Analysis
topics: Performance Analysis – Time and Space Complexity

modules.title: Divide and Conquer Strategy
topics: Binary Search, Merge Sort, and Quick Sort
Analysis of Divide and Conquer Algorithms

modules.title: Greedy Method and Dynamic Programming
topics: Optimal Merge Patterns, Huffman Coding, Minimum Spanning Tree (Kruskal's and Prim's)

modules.title: Complexity Theory and NP Problems
topics: Introduction to P, NP, NP-Hard, and NP-Complete Classes

suggested_books: Ellis Horowitz, Sartaj Sahni, Sanguthevar Rajasekaran, Fundamentals of Computer Algorithms, Galgotia Publications
Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest, Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th Edition, MIT Press
reference_books: Jon Kleinberg and Éva Tardos, Algorithm Design, Pearson
Anany Levitin, Introduction to the Design and Analysis of Algorithms, Pearson
